content_html:
Intention as Probabilistic Autonomy

Free will, intention, is fundamentally a probabilistic process. Self-aware, but nonetheless autonomous?

Claim: Intention is the self-aware modulation of probabilistic dynamics. The brain never makes all-or-nothing jumps; it performs graded competitions among partial hypotheses about what to do next. Intention is the system’s ability to bias those competitions in line with goals, norms, and identity.

Intention is awareness guiding probability toward meaning—freedom as practiced bias.
Autonomy is shaped uncertainty.

From Noise to Intention

  • Noise → Exploration: stochastic fluctuations allow flexible trialing of action tendencies.
  • Structure → Constraint: learned models and values prune the space of viable options.
  • Feedback → Autonomy: recurrent loops (perception–prediction–action) stabilize preferred policies.

Working definition: Probabilistic autonomy is a self that determines how it will be determined — it shapes the conditions under which certain outcomes become likely, without stepping outside causality.

Self-awareness as Meta-Probability

Awareness does not hand-pick outcomes; it refines the model that sets their odds. Each episode of attention updates priors and reweights cues, so that tomorrow’s “likely” already reflects what was cared about today.

Mapping to Select – Change – Reconstruct

  • Select: attend to a subset of cues; commit computational resources to preferred hypotheses.
  • Change: act and learn; plasticity converts successful biasing into trait-like dispositions.
  • Reconstruct: narrate the choice into identity (“this is what I do when it matters”), feeding back as a constraint on future probabilities.
